title: The collector's quiet obsession
text: {{1}} people collect is a question psychologists have answered several times over: control in a small kingdom, memory made physical, and the deep pleasure of completion. Collecting ranges {{2}} stamps to vintage synthesizers, but the shape of the obsession is always {{3}} same. {{4}} is the hunt that delivers the sharpest pleasure — the auction won, the gap filled — and {{5}} a set is complete, many collectors quietly begin the search all over again. A collection is never really finished; {{6}} is always one more piece. The hobby has survived every technology that was supposed to kill it; {{7}} anything, the digital archive has made the rare find rarer still. What looks like clutter from outside is, from inside, {{8}} ordered world with the collector's name written all over it.

gaps.explanation: Fronted subject clause asking the reason: Why people collect.
'Range from X to Y' — the first element takes 'from'.
'The same' is the fixed definite phrase.

gaps.explanation: The cleft structure emphasises the hunt.
'Once' — as soon as the completion happens.
